newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul traders group sees '97 trade deficit falling.
newsitem.headline: Seoul traders group sees '97 trade deficit falling.

text.p: South Korea is expected to run a trade deficit of $18 billion in calendar 1997, down from an estimated shortfall of $20 billion this year, the Korea International Trade Association said on Monday.

A statement from the association, formerly the Korea Foreign Trade Association, forecast customs-cleared exports to rise by nine percent to $142 billion in 1997 from this year's estimated $130 billion exports.
Customs-cleared imports were forecast to grow by seven percent to $160 billion in 1997 from this year's estimated $150 billion, the statement said.
Exports of heavy-industrial and chemical products were expected to increase 12 percent to $103.7 billion in 1997, following an estimated 2.0 percent growth in 1996, it said.
Light-industrial exports are expected to see a recovery, growing by three percent to $28.7 billion in 1997 after an estimated one-percent decline to $27.9 billion this year, the statement said.
The statement said estimates for this year's exports and imports were up by four percent and 11 percent, respectively, from 1995.
Exports of petroleum products, industrial electronic equipment, automobiles, tyre and electronic parts excluding semiconductors are expected to remain bullish, it said.

The nation's trade deficit with its three largest partners -- the United States, Japan and the European Union -- is expected to widen to $43 billion in 1997 from this year's estimated shortfall of $41.5 billion, the statement said.
But South Korea will see its trade surplus with other partners expanding to $25 billion in 1997 from this year's estimated surplus of $21.5 billion, it said.
